user.title: Choose the backend data source
user.description: The existing Home Assistant UniFi integration is recommended and does not create another controller session. The separate login is an explicit fallback.

menu_option_descriptions.official: Reuse the live controller sessions and permissions already managed by Home Assistant.
menu_option_descriptions.direct: Create a dedicated backend-only controller session. Choose this only when the official integration cannot provide the required data.

reconfigure.title: Change the backend data source
reconfigure.description: Changing the source reloads only this companion integration. It does not create, replace, or edit dashboard cards.

menu_option_descriptions.official: Stop using separate backend credentials and reuse Home Assistant's loaded UniFi sessions.
menu_option_descriptions.direct: Validate and save a dedicated controller login for this backend only.

official.title: Use Home Assistant's UniFi integration
official.description: Found {controller_count} configured UniFi controller(s), of which {loaded_count} are currently loaded. The backend automatically matches a requested device to the correct loaded controller. No credentials are copied and no second session is created.

data_description.diagnostics_enabled: Diagnostics contain source status and object counts, but never controller credentials, client names, IP addresses, or MAC addresses.

direct.title: Separate UniFi login fallback
direct.description: This creates a dedicated controller session only after you explicitly select this fallback. Credentials remain in Home Assistant's backend config entry and are never sent to the card. Use a local UniFi account; administrator rights are required only for write actions such as PoE cycling and Etherlighting.

data_description.host: Local IP address or hostname of the UniFi console or Network application.
data_description.username: A local UniFi account is recommended.
data_description.password: Stored only in Home Assistant's config entry. It is redacted from diagnostics.
data_description.verify_ssl: Enable this only when the controller certificate is trusted by Home Assistant.
data_description.diagnostics_enabled: Diagnostics contain status and counts, not credentials or network identities.

site.title: Select the UniFi site
site.description: Choose the site the card backend should read from through this dedicated login.

init.title: Backend status and diagnostics
init.description: Current source: `{source}`. Home Assistant has {controller_count} configured official UniFi controller(s), of which {loaded_count} are loaded. To change the source or direct-login credentials, use **Reconfigure** on the integration. Dashboard cards are never modified automatically.

data_description.diagnostics_enabled: When disabled, downloaded diagnostics contain only this setting, the selected source, and entry state.
